source.title: The Striatum Organizes 3D Behavior via Moment-to-Moment Action Selection.

confidence_rationale: High-quality cellular recording + lesion study (Cell, Datta/Sabatini) showing the dorsolateral striatum encodes the identity and ordering of a discrete repertoire of sub-second 3D behavioral motifs and is required to assemble them into sequences. Directly evidences a structured behavioral-MODULE repertoire that the basal ganglia selects over -- the closest biological analog to MECH-442's behavioral-descriptor archive. Capped because the result is about sequence COMPOSITION over a module set, not per-niche-elite preservation against a value argmax.
failure_signatures: The striatum encodes module identity/ordering and assembles sequences, but the paper does not show per-niche-elite preservation through a value-maximizing selection -- it evidences a repertoire + selection-over-it, not diversity surviving a strong reward gradient.

Module selection here is facilitated by fast direct/indirect-pathway decorrelation (a competitive gating), consistent with a winner-take-all commit rather than simultaneous multi-niche retention at the output.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Dorsolateral striatum (DLS) neurons in the direct and indirect pathways systematically encode the identity and ordering of sub-second 3D behavioral motifs (modules); fast-timescale decorrelation between pathways facilitates this encoding, and DLS lesions prevent appropriate behavioral-sequence assembly.
mapping.ree_translation: A structured repertoire of discrete behavioral modules, indexed and selected by the basal ganglia, is a real biological object -- the closest analog to MECH-442's behavioral-descriptor archive over candidate actions. It supports the existence of a behavioral-module store the committed selection draws from, locating that store in the striatal action-selection machinery rather than only at the final argmax.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The study evidences a behavioral-module repertoire and selection/composition over it, NOT the specific MECH-442 property that behaviorally-distinct modules are RETAINED (per-niche elites) against a strong value gradient at the commit; pathway decorrelation here looks more like competitive winner-take-all gating than simultaneous per-niche retention.
mapping.source_context: Freely-moving mice; 3D depth-imaging behavioral motif segmentation (MoSeq); DLS bulk + cellular photometry across direct/indirect pathways; DLS NMDA lesions.

confidence_components.notes: Strong methods + venue; mapping_fidelity moderate because it shows a repertoire + selection-over-it (the archive EXISTS and BG selects from it) but not per-niche-elite retention against a value argmax; transfer_risk moderate (rodent spontaneous behavior to E3 committed trajectory selection).
